title: Gluten-Free Vanilla Coconut Cupcakes
shortDescription: Light gluten-free cupcakes with coconut milk batter and a vanilla swirl frosting, ready in about 45 minutes.
description: These cupcakes use coconut milk instead of regular milk, so the crumb stays soft and a little tender. I tested this batch three times in my own kitchen to get the rise right without gluten. The batter smells like vanilla and toasted coconut before it even hits the oven. A gluten-free flour blend with xanthan gum keeps the texture close to a classic cupcake, not dense or gritty. The frosting gets a swirl of extra vanilla paste for little flecks you can see. Top with toasted coconut flakes for crunch and a bakery look. This recipe works well for guests with gluten sensitivities who still want a normal-tasting cupcake. Nobody will guess it is gluten-free.
ingredients: 1 3/4 cups gluten-free all-purpose flour blend (with xanthan gum)
3/4 cup full-fat coconut milk (canned, well shaken)
1 cup unsalted butter, softened, for frosting
1 tsp vanilla bean paste, for frosting
1/3 cup toasted coconut flakes, for topping
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk the gluten-free flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a bowl.
Beat butter and sugar together for 2 minutes until light and fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each. Mix in vanilla and coconut extract.
Add the flour mix in three parts, alternating with coconut milk. Mix just until smooth.
Fold in the shredded coconut by hand with a spatula.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a rack.
Beat frosting butter until smooth, about 1 minute. Add powdered sugar in two batches.
Mix in coconut milk and vanilla bean paste until the frosting is smooth and pipeable.
Pipe a tall swirl onto each cooled cupcake. Press toasted coconut flakes onto the sides.
tips: Shake the canned coconut milk well before measuring so fat and liquid blend evenly.
Let cupcakes cool fully before frosting, or the swirl will slide off.
Toast the coconut flakes in a dry pan over low heat for 3 minutes, watching closely so they do not burn.
Check your gluten-free flour blend label. Some already include xanthan gum, others need it added separately.

faq.question: Can I use coconut cream instead of coconut milk in the batter?
faq.answer: Use full-fat canned coconut milk, not coconut cream. Coconut cream is too thick and will make the batter heavy.

faq.question: Why did my gluten-free cupcakes sink in the middle?
faq.answer: This usually means the batter was overmixed or the oven door opened too early. Mix just until smooth and check at 16 minutes, not before.

faq.question: Can I make these dairy-free too?
faq.answer: Swap the butter for a vegan butter stick in both cake and frosting. The coconut milk already covers the dairy-free milk swap.

faq.question: How long do these cupcakes stay fresh?
faq.answer: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for 2 days, or in the fridge for 4 days. Bring to room temperature before serving.

conclusion: These cupcakes prove gluten-free baking can still taste rich and soft. Keep the coconut milk cold and shaken, and do not overmix the batter. Serve them at a spring party or any day you want something light but still sweet.
